name: Caption
text: The desktop sidebar: 248px wide, 16px padding, a soft right border and no brand block. Five links (For You, Your Songs, Wallet, Notifications, Profile), a Communities section, a Moderator section when the viewer moderates something, and the account row pinned to the bottom behind a divider. The account row shows the profile in use and opens the account menu (Parts/Shell/AppShellChrome), per the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12; its second line, the profile's community, is the design agent's choice. Notifications carries a dot when something is unread, and never when signed out. The create-community plus belongs to the Communities header row, right-aligned and centred on the label; it is never a standalone button. Links are 40px rows with 12px radius; community rows are 44px with a 24px coloured avatar. There is no Post here: a post belongs to a community, so Post lives on the community page.

name: Caption
text: The shared pieces that screens and flows are built from: each is drawn once here and cloned everywhere else. A filled circle is drawn, an open circle is to draw. A drawn master does not change its copies; each copy is edited and viewed when its flow is next touched.

name: Caption
text: New design, not in the code. Tapping a reward pill in the feed opens this: a Modal on desktop and a bottom sheet on phone, built on the Modal pattern with no footer. Rewards belong to activities, so there is one Item row per activity and nothing else: the activity and the pills for exactly what it pays, in the same colours as the feed. Tapping a row starts the activity. Here Karaoke pays the lottery share, the bonus and the token; Study pays the lottery share and the token; Dance pays the token only. Pills stay on one line. Qualification (the score an activity needs) is deliberately not shown here, per the workspace_owner; it belongs inside the activity. Not drawn: claimed, exhausted, entry closed and blocked states, the streak strip, and the pool disclosures the spec requires one tap away. Source: docs/design/rewards-ui.md, Surface A, and Spec 015.

name: Caption
text: The one post card, used wherever a post is listed: the community page, a profile, a single post. Three kinds share one frame. The author row is the same on all: avatar, handle, age, and the overflow menu. The body is the kind: text shows a title and body, a song shows its tile with a play button, a video shows its poster. The action row is the same on all, built from the VotePill and CommentPill patterns, with a third pill for rewards when the post has a song (Parts/Rewards/RewardPill). The pill is deliberately minimal, per the workspace_owner: the gift mark and a number, in the same shape as the comment pill. The number is how many activities the song offers; it is not money and never says the viewer has earned anything. Tapping it opens Parts/Rewards/SongEarnSheet. A text post has no song, so no rewards pill. Design change from the code: the video kind and the rewards pill are new; the app's card handles text and song only, and puts a Boost button in the author row instead. Source: features/community/page-shell (CommunityPostCard) and features/posts/shared-engagement.

name: Caption
text: New design. One sheet for every identity check, so joining, viewing 18+ content and claiming winnings all work the same way: a Modal on desktop, a bottom sheet on phone, opened over the page the viewer is on. The title is what they are doing ("Join Harbor Collective", "Claim 12 USDC", "Verify you're 18+"); the one line under it is how. On desktop the body is a QR code to scan with the phone app. On phone there is no QR, only one button that opens the app. A check that accepts two apps (nationality and age: Self or ZKPassport) shows the two choices first. While the app is open the sheet waits; when the proof arrives the sheet closes and the action finishes by itself, with no second tap and no separate page. If the viewer has no public identity for the community yet, the same sheet asks "Joining as" before it closes. Design change from the code: today the palm scan leaves for a separate page that never returns to the community, the document check is a different modal that needs Join tapped again afterwards, and the phone shows a QR while the desktop does not. Source: routes/verify/very.tsx, features/verification/document-verification-host.tsx, features/rewards/wallet-winnings.tsx.

name: Caption
text:
Under review, not yet approved. The end of every activity: Dance, Study, Karaoke.
Dance ends on one page. A mark, a title, one line naming the song and the day the take was sent, the rewards for that activity, and one footer button. Dance says Submitted, because the community's owner checks it later, and a dance joins the lottery of the day it passes, per the workspace_owner, so its lottery row says only what winning means: no amount, no count and no timer, because nothing is earned yet and the drawing it will join is not known. Its rows sit under "If your dance passes, you get". The page says nothing about whether the take will be public; the workspace_owner removed that line on 2026-10-12 as unnecessary, since the choice is made on Review just before.
The same pages are where the dancer looks later, by two routes, per the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12. From a notification (Screens/Shell/Notifications): the row "Your dance passed" opens Passed, "Your dance didn't pass" opens Not passed, and "Your dance wasn't reviewed" opens Not reviewed. And from the Your take row on the dance's own page (Flows/Dance/Take): In review opens Submitted, and the other three states open their result. No list of a person's takes is drawn. Passed shows what was earned, as the same cards the Rewards page uses, and one line giving the day that counts toward the streak; when the dance carried no reward, Passed shows the streak line alone. Not passed says so and offers Try again. Not reviewed is the fourth ending: nobody checked the take within seven days of upload, per the workspace_owner on 2026-09-30. It has a neutral mark, says plainly that it is not a fail, and offers Try again, which starts a new attempt. Withdraw take, proposed: a quiet action under Done on the waiting Submitted page, with a confirmation, drawn beside Submitted. It carries forward the withdrawn state in the 2026-09-30 draft; the placement is the reviewer's recommendation. It exists only while the take is waiting and never undoes an answer. Every date on these pages is written out, never "today", so an old result still reads true when reopened. The passed states and the song line were added on 2026-10-12 on the reviewer's recommendation. A dance counting toward the streak for the day it was sent was accepted by the workspace_owner that day.
Study and Karaoke end on up to three pages, one after another, as Duolingo does: Result, then Streak, then Rewards. Each page has one job and Continue moves on; the repeat action (Study again, Sing again) sits only on the last page, beside Done, because offering it earlier would skip the pages that follow.
Result always appears: the headline for the score band and the score as one large number, nothing else. Streak appears only when this activity earned today's streak day: the flame, the number, the words "day streak" (never a bare number) and the week. Rewards appears only when the person earned something: one separate card per reward, each with the same three lines (what it is, what they got, a short note), a colour bar for the kind (gold for the lottery, green for a cash bonus), then Study again and Done. The streak comes before the rewards so the page that most often applies is first and the surprise is last.
Lottery wording, the same for Dance, Study and Karaoke, confirmed by the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12. The card reads "Daily lottery", "You're entered", then "Drawing on 11 October. If the ticket wins, you get part of the prize." It never shows a count, because a person is entered in a drawing once and another qualifying attempt adds nothing. Rejected that day: "1 entry" (miscounts), "Share confirmed" (not coherent English, and "share" read as sharing the take), "You're in" (not understood by ordinary people). The word "share" is not used on these pages. Keep reward copy to one short sentence; the workspace_owner called a two-sentence row verbose.
Which rewards a passed dance can show is not settled: the 2026-09-30 rulings limit an owner-reviewed pass to rewards funded by that community or the song's owner, never platform-funded pools, and require the dancer's human verification; the Dance pages here draw the daily lottery and a bonus. That is for the Spec 021 amendment to reconcile, and the passed page promises nothing until it does.
Routing after the Result, proposed. While the lottery answer is loading the Result shows "Checking the lottery…" and Continue is held; this is a waiting state, never an ending. Nobody is made to wait: a close mark at the top left leaves at once. If the check fails or runs out of time, the Result says "Couldn't check the lottery. Try again." with Try again and Done. Try again repeats the status check only; it never sends the activity again. The app's status reader already gives up after 15 seconds (features/rewards/megapot-participant), which is the reference for "out of time". Unresolved: after leaving, or after Done on the failed state, there is no designed place to check later whether the person was entered. The Wallet shows winnings, not entries, and being entered and winning are different things. Whatever was earned is still recorded by the server; only the way to see an entry afterwards is missing. The code's own words for the wait are "Checking your share…". Once the answer is in: if a streak day or any reward was newly earned, Continue goes on to Streak and Rewards as usual. The Result is the final page, with Study again and Done, only when there is nothing further to show, and then it carries one quiet line. "No lottery reward from this attempt." when the song has a reward and this attempt earned none; it speaks of the attempt only and so cannot read as removing an entry already held. "You're already entered in the 11 October drawing." when an earlier attempt already entered the person and this one earned no new streak day and no cash reward. If the person is already entered but did earn a new streak day or a cash reward, those pages follow and the already-entered line is not an ending; how the Rewards page then words the lottery is not drawn. The server knows why nothing was earned (below the score floor, entries closed, or no drawing open); the page does not say which.
Streaks are per song and per community, counted by day in the account's own timezone, and a streak day is earned by a qualifying activity, not by finishing (Spec 015 section 7). The page shows the song streak.
Design change from the code: the app's ActivityResults shows the score and two or three tiles, then a reward slot, and its Study streak page replaces the score page. This keeps the score, drops the tiles, drops the song name on Study and Karaoke (Dance keeps it, because its result is read later, away from the song), and puts streak and rewards on their own pages.
Not drawn: the message when a withdrawal loses the race to an answer, the Rewards page for someone already entered who earned a cash reward, a place to check a lottery entry later, claiming a cash reward, a second line for the community streak, desktop.
Source: features/activity/activity-results, features/studying, features/karaoke, features/rewards/megapot-participant; Spec 015 sections 3 and 7; docs/design/rewards-ui.md; the pool fields in api-next rewards-song-offers.

Phone: Dance submitted; the same with "Cancel review", and its confirmation (proposed); Dance passed (with rewards, then with none); Dance not passed; Dance not reviewed. The last three are opened from Notifications (Screens/Shell/Notifications): the row "Your dance passed" opens Passed, "Your dance didn't pass" opens Not passed, and "Your dance wasn't reviewed" opens Not reviewed.
Words, per the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12: no screen says "take"; most people won't understand it and it won't translate well. What a person sent is "your video", and what they cancel is the review, not the dance: "Cancel this dance" was tried and could read as removing the original dance. This wording is the reviewer's proposal and is not yet confirmed by the workspace_owner. Notes here still say take or attempt where they need to tell one recording from the dance it copies; those words are for builders only.
Cancelling a review: carried forward from the 2026-09-30 draft, which calls the state withdrawn; this placement is the reviewer's recommendation, not a ruling. A quiet "Cancel review" under Done on the waiting Submitted page, then a confirmation with Cancel review and Keep waiting. It exists only while the video is waiting. Nothing changes on screen until the server confirms: only then does the "Your video" row leave the dance's page and Do this dance come back. Three other outcomes, kept apart. A confirmed failure: the server says it did not happen, the video is still in review, and the person can try again. An unknown outcome: the request went out and no answer came back, so it may or may not be cancelled; another attempt stays unavailable, and the app reads the status again or sends the same request again, which must be safe to repeat, then shows whatever the server confirms: cancelled, still in review, or already answered. An answer that got there first: a pass, a fail or the seven-day expiry stands and its result is shown; cancelling never undoes an answer. Removing the row after a confirmed cancel is the design agent's choice, not a ruling: the server keeps the record, and the page must not then show an older attempt as if it were the latest. Not drawn: the confirmed failure with retry, the unknown outcome, and the message when the answer got there first.
Not reviewed: seven days from upload with no answer, per the workspace_owner on 2026-09-30. It is final, like a pass or a fail: it is never reviewed later and never restored. Try again, here and on Not passed, starts a new attempt at the same dance from the camera; it never reopens the old one

name: Caption
text:
Under review, not yet approved. New design, built from the Boost screens.
One payment step for everything the app sells or funds: Boost now, and handles, songs and videos later (Spec 012 keeps paid handles disabled for now).
What each purchase supplies: the rows above From on Review, the amount, the address the server says to pay, and its own final message in place of Paid. Everything else is shared: Confirm, the From and Fee rows, the Pay button, Sending, and the two problem screens.
How it pays, from the code and Specs 004 and 014. The money moves from the persona's own wallet to platform custody as one USDC transfer that the wallet signs in the browser; the server only watches the chain. From names that persona and the short wallet address. Confirm appears only when the wallet is locked: a short sign-in, an email code in this sketch, unlocks it for five minutes, and then Review loads the balance and the fee.
Paying from an external address is not in version one. A person who holds funds elsewhere sends them to this wallet's address first (Wallet, Receive), which is what Add USDC opens. Paying straight from an external wallet would need the server to accept another payer, and I read Spec 014 as treating a wallet that links a persona to something else as a privacy problem, so it is a later decision. The From row is where a choice would go.
The fee is paid in ETH from the same wallet, so a wallet with USDC and no ETH cannot pay. Can't pay the fee exists only if the app does not cover the fee. Covering it, as the winnings send does with its gas top-up, is the better answer and removes that screen and the Fee row; the workspace_owner has not decided.
After Pay: Sending, then the purchase's own result. A failure that says nothing was sent offers another try. Not drawn: the wallet may have sent it and the status is unknown, the transfer reverted, and the five minutes running out; the code handles all three in text today.
Testnet only today: the transfer is Base Sepolia test USDC. Mainnet is separate work.
Source: api/reward-wallet-session.ts; features/rewards (reward-funding-panel, reward-sponsor-dialog); features/wallet (receive and send sheets); Specs 004, 012 §5.3.7 and 014.

text:
Under review. A list of label and value pairs. Two kinds share the alignment and nothing else.
Review rows are read-only: what a person is about to confirm, or what just happened. Nothing in the row can be tapped.
Settings rows do something: open an editor, flip a switch, or copy a value. The right end of the row shows which.
Shared: label at the left, value at the right, 16px type, 14px above and below, a hairline between rows and none after the last. No filled card behind the rows. A long value wraps under itself and stays right-aligned; an address or hash is shortened in the middle, never wrapped. The label never wraps: shorten the label.

text:
Under review. The third pill on a song post, after votes and comments. It does one thing: opens that song's rewards sheet (Parts/Rewards/SongEarnSheet), which is where Study, Karaoke and Dance start. It is the only way into them from a post (workspace_owner, 2026-10-11).
The number is how many activities the song offers. It is not money, not a count of rewards, and never says the viewer has earned anything. Earning is shown only on the result screens (Parts/Rewards/ActivityResult) and in the Wallet.
A post with no song has no pill; it is left out, not greyed.
Same height, radius and outline as VotePill and CommentPill (Patterns/Engagement).

text:
Under review. Three things show a song in a row. They share the left half and differ on purpose in the rest, so this is one shared piece and three rows, not one row with switches.
Shared: square artwork with the medium radius, then the title in the text colour at medium weight, then one muted line under it. The title is cut with an ellipsis; the muted line is too.
Song list row (Screens/Songs/YourSongs): the muted line is the artist. The whole row opens the song's sheet. It carries the person's own progress on that song.
Song tile on a post (Parts/Posts/PostCard): an outlined box inside the post. The muted line is the artist. Its one action is Play, at the right. Tapping the rest does nothing here; activities start from the reward pill below the post.
Moderation row (Screens/Community/Management, Queue): this is a submission, not a song. The artwork slot is the dancer's video still, taller than wide. The title is the song; the muted line is the dancer's handle, then how long it has waited. The row opens the review.
Data gap for the moderation row: the moderation contract today lists text posts, comments and replies, and gives the author's profile id, not a public handle. It has no dance queue. The row is design; its data source is not built.
What must not be merged: Play belongs only to the tile; progress belongs only to the list row; waiting time and the dancer belong only to the moderation row.
Instances looked at: the three below, copied from those sheets. All six Queue rows on Screens/Community/Management carry the dancer. Not rechecked: the song picker in Flows/Posts/Song and Flows/Posts/Video.

name: Caption
text:
Under review. How many days in a row a person has done enough. Four forms of the same thing.
Compact: a flame and the number, with the week beside it. Used at the top of a song's sheet (Screens/Songs/YourSongs).
Completion: the flame large, the number, "day streak", and the week under it. Its own screen after an activity's result (Parts/Rewards/ActivityResult).
Week strip: seven marks, Monday to Sunday, filled for days that counted. Today is outlined until it counts.
Leaderboard: rank, profile and current streak, with the viewer's own place as the last row. One list serves a song and a community, and it has its own page, drawn in the last group.
Where each leaderboard opens from, approved by the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12: on a song, a Leaderboard action on a line under the song streak; on a community, a line above the feed with the viewer's community streak and a Leaderboard action. Both are drawn here and in place on their own sheets.
One streak for every activity, per the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12: Study, Karaoke and Dance all feed the same streak. The completion screen follows Study and Karaoke; both flows draw it on the phone. Dance has no completion screen, because its result comes later. Not built: the server's streak writer takes Study and Karaoke only, and Dance is reserved and not wired.
Two facts that must stay apart. "Qualified today" says the day already counts, whenever that happened. "This completion newly earned today" says the activity just finished is the one that made it count. The compact form and the week strip follow the first. The completion screen follows only the second: a person who qualified this morning and finishes another activity tonight sees the result and no streak screen. Do not light today because an activity ended.
Accepted by the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12, loosely ("sound reasonable"): an attempt that finishes below the target does not count, as today, so no streak screen follows one. A dance counts for the day it was sent, once it passes: a waiting take earns nothing yet, and passing fills in the original day.
Scope: the server stores two streaks, one per song and one per community, both kept against the account, and has a leaderboard for each (top 100 by current streak, plus the viewer's own place). The workspace_owner wants both levels working, as a ranking inside a community. The app calls neither leaderboard. They are separate from the Karaoke score leaderboard the app already has.
Missing support, kept apart from the design. The app's current Study screen does not hand the display any streak fields; the older Study display had the count and qualified-today. The contracts read in this pass do not carry seven daily marks, so the week strip has no data behind it. Nothing read reports "newly earned" as its own field.
Instances looked at: the compact and completion forms below, copied from their sheets. Not rechecked: Flows/Studying/Session and Flows/Karaoke/Practice. Not drawn: either leaderboard entry on desktop, the leaderboard page on desktop, and its empty, loading and failed states.

name: Caption
text:
Under review. The block that says where something stands: a mark, a heading, an explanation, and what can be done. It shares spacing and order, not length. A simple state is a heading and a line; a recovery state may carry evidence, a deadline and two actions, and that is right when both actions are real.
Order, top to bottom: mark (40px), 16px, heading (20px, semibold), 8px, explanation (16px, muted), then any evidence as rows (Parts/Rows/ReviewRows), then any deadline as its own line, 24px, then actions, the main one first.
Six states that must stay apart, by mark and by words, never by colour alone.
Waiting: we are doing something or watching for something. A ring. It never looks finished.
Uncertain: we cannot tell what happened, such as a wallet send with no answer. A question mark. It says what is being checked and never guesses.
Held: nothing is moving; something is kept safe until a condition is met. A pause mark. A hold can have a problem behind it, so the block says why when it is known.
Recoverable: something needs the person to act, and acting can still fix this same attempt. An exclamation mark. It carries the action, and any evidence or deadline that bears on it. It is never worded as a failure.
Failed: this attempt ended. A cross. It says so without claiming more than is known, and it may offer a way on, including starting another valid attempt.
Done: it worked. A tick.
"Sent" and "Paid" are both Done and are different facts: Sent is an outgoing transfer, Paid is a confirmed reward payment. Sharing this layout does not make the words interchangeable. Nothing is called Paid before the payment is confirmed.
Two forms. The block form above is for a dialog, a sheet or a whole screen. The page-card form is for a settings page holding several at once: no mark, a small line naming the subject, the same order of heading, explanation, evidence and deadline, and actions at the right with the main one last.
Instances checked. Block form: Sent (Flows/Wallet/Send), Dance submitted (Parts/Rewards/ActivityResult), the claim rows and the verification page states (Flows/Wallet/Claim), the handle and Spaces dialogs (Flows/Community/JoinAndName). Page-card form: the Address cards in groups 2, 3, 5 and 10 (Flows/Community/Address) were viewed against this and keep that order, with their evidence and actions unchanged; the other Address groups were not re-viewed.

text:
Under review. The frame around a page: the desktop sidebar (Parts/Shell/AppSidebar), the phone footer (Patterns/Navigation/MobileFooterNav) and the phone page header (Patterns/Navigation/MobilePageHeader). Those sheets draw each piece. This sheet says which pages get which, and nothing here redraws them, with one exception: the account menu and Settings below.
Destinations. Five on the phone: Home, Your Songs, Wallet, Notifications, Profile. The app has four, with a bell in the header in place of the Notifications tab, so the app's shell needs the tab added. On 2026-10-12 the tab was taken out of Paper for a few hours and then put back: the workspace_owner expected Notifications in the footer. No header bell is drawn. Neither a tab nor a bell supplies what is missing behind it: the app's Notifications page reads "Notifications are unavailable" and the server stores none.
Account row, per the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12: the sidebar's bottom row shows the profile in use and opens one menu: the person's profiles, Settings, Sign out. The second line of the row, the profile's community, is the design agent's choice and not part of the ruling. The row on Parts/Shell/AppSidebar and the sidebar copies on other sheets show the same row.
On a phone, approved by the workspace_owner the same day: the More button on your own profile opens the menu as a sheet, keeping Share, and Settings is a plain page reached from either menu, with Telegram, Recordings, Terms and Privacy. Both are drawn below, with the Recordings page and its confirmation. Not drawn: Settings on desktop.
Fixed chrome and content. The phone header is fixed at the top and the footer at the bottom, so a page's content starts below the header and ends above the footer, each with the device's safe area added; the app does this with the top and bottom safe-area insets. A page with an action bar puts the bar above the safe area and the footer is gone. A sheet's own bottom padding includes the safe area. Toasts sit above the footer. Check on every new phone page that the last item can scroll clear of whatever is fixed at the bottom.
Instances looked at in this pass: the Wallet, the profile page, the post page, Management and its section pages, the Address phone route. The Paper frames do not draw a status bar or a home indicator, so safe areas are stated here and not visible in the drawings.

name: Caption
text:
Words: the address a person gets under the community's name space is a handle; the display name on a profile is a name. Every string here says handle. A Spaces community gives name@community instead and says name.
Join makes the person a member and a follower at once, with no handle needed. The handle sheet opens right after, on the community's own host: one field ending in the community's root, a length hint, and Get handle, disabled until the input is valid. Pressing Get handle is the confirmation that the handle is public; there is no checkbox and no notice.
Closing the sheet keeps membership. A missing, pending or failed handle never blocks posting, Study or Karaoke, and a returning member is never prompted. Until a handle is chosen the member shows everywhere as "User" and six characters, for example User 4KQ7M2.
A profile is labelled by its handle if it has one, otherwise its name, otherwise that User label.
One handle per member in a community, to start, and it cannot be replaced once issued, per the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12 (for now). The owner's offer must say one; today it sends no limit, which is a known defect.
The sheet exists only when the community's address is on, handles are on and requests are open (Flows/Community/Address, group 8).
Issued and working are separate: a handle can be issued while its page is not opening. The old "unfinished" sheet is replaced by that state. The journey branch still refuses to show a handle as issued until its page opens; that is a defect in its controller, not only in the words.
How long issuing takes is not promised.
Spaces: members only; the name is held by a Bitcoin key we make for the profile, set up by an email code, and an unclear setup checks the one already there before making another. A pending name is a request, not a name: it can end without the name, so no sheet says it is yours until it is written and settled, and a failed one does not say the name is free again. No time is promised. Staging only today.
Coming back is not all restored. The last group says what each return relies on, checked against code, and marks the two that nothing built covers.
To draw: the profile picker for Handshake handles; getting a first profile ready; failing before joining; desktop.

Mirror of the Storybook flow Flows/Studying/Session (src/features/studying/studying-surface), phone only, with design changes listed below.
One card at a time under the shared activity header: a close mark and a progress bar. The mark is a close, not a back arrow, because cards cannot be revisited: there is no previous screen to go back to. It leaves at once with no confirmation, because leaving loses nothing: the lesson's session is kept for 24 hours and opening the song's Study again in the same browser continues at the same card (Spec 019 section 4.1; the start coordinator reuses a session that is still active). There is no resume screen, per the no-drafts rule. Say it back asks the learner to record the line; the footer button is the only control and changes with the phase: Record, Stop, Checking, then the result. Multiple choice has four option cards and no footer until an answer is given.
Both card types end the same way: one result box under the card content, a coloured border and tint. Correct is green with a check and says Correct. Incorrect is red with a cross and says Incorrect; in say it back, a line under it, the full width of the box, says "You said: ..." with what was heard, and it may run to two lines. In multiple choice the chosen option also turns green or red and the right answer is shown.
What happens next. The workspace_owner said on 2026-10-12: "our study shows a continue button - this is wrong, if right, it just goes to the next exercise. incorrect should pause so they can see what's wrong." Incorrect pausing is plainly ruled. Correct going on by itself with no Continue is the design agent's reading of the first half. Drawn so: a correct answer shows Correct and the next card follows without a button; an incorrect answer stops and waits for Continue, in say it back and in multiple choice alike. The app already behaves close to this: a correct spoken answer moves on at once, a correct choice after 700 milliseconds, and a spoken miss is final for that appearance, with the card coming back later if the server chooses. So there is no Record-again on a miss; an earlier drawing offered one and it was removed.

The last group is the end of the lesson, drawn as the pages in order: Result (headline and score), Streak, Rewards, and the Result variant when the song has a reward and this attempt earned none. text:
Claim a pool win from the Wallet (Spec 015 §5.2a). The Wallet shows one profile, so every win listed belongs to that profile and is paid to that profile's wallet; nothing is chosen or redirected.
A claim is one action on one win. With one win, the Rewards card's Claim opens it. With several, each win is its own row with its own Claim.

Each claim is checked by the server by itself; nothing claims several wins at once. The sheet says "You need a palm scan before you can claim." and the button is "Scan palm"; the verification page itself names the Very app, since that is where the person needs it.
Coming back from a palm scan opens the Wallet on the profile that earned the win, with that win in view, whichever profile was showing before. The app resumes the win but does not switch to its profile, so the result can be hidden; that is a defect to fix in code.
Claimed is not paid. After a claim is accepted the win shows Claimed while the profile's wallet is set up, while it is sending, and while a failed send is retried; it shows Paid only when the payment is confirmed. At Paid the wallet's balance is read again and the payment is in it; the reward amount is never added on top, which would count it twice. A stalled payment is retried against the same claim and never asks for another scan.
On hold means the claim could not be completed and the amount is held; it is never shown as a success. A claim refused for a missing or stale palm scan leaves the win unclaimed, with Claim still there.

Getting here: a song's sheet has a Dance row beside Study and Karaoke, in Your songs (Screens/Songs/YourSongs) and in the rewards sheet opened from a post's pill (Parts/Rewards/SongEarnSheet). The row opens the song's dances.
Choosing an existing dance: a song has a page of its dances, a grid of videos, two across, that scrolls. The first tile is a plus, which starts a new dance. Tiles carry no handle, per the workspace_owner: people choose a dance for what it pays. A dance that pays has one pill in the feed's colours; one that pays nothing has none, and those come last. When a dance pays both a cash bonus and the lottery, the tile shows the cash bonus, which is the amount that tells dances apart; the lottery appears on the dance page. Two across, not three, because a pill does not fit on a three-across tile. A funder can attach a reward to any dance of a song or to one exact dance (Spec 021), so tiles can differ.
Tapping a dance opens it full screen and plays it, so the person watches a dance before deciding. This is its own page, not the Home feed: no bottom navigation and no action rail, only the video, who made it, all the dance's rewards, the arrow back to the grid, and one button, "Do this dance". A dance can only be chosen from here, after it has been watched. The next and previous dances are a swipe away. Tapping a pill would open the rewards sheet, as in the feed.
The camera is the same camera as a video post, with Upload at the bottom left.
Review is full screen and has one choice and one button. The choice is a switch, "Show publicly if it passes", on by default, per the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12, because public dances are what grows the site. Inside the same card, under the label, a second line says "Same rewards either way."; the workspace_owner asked for it to sit with the switch, not apart from it. The button is "Submit for review"; it sends the take and saves the choice. The switch stood on the Submitted page until that day, where a switch followed by Done read as if Done posted the take; the workspace_owner questioned it and it was moved here.
On desktop the same steps are cards in the main column, in order, above the phone screens: the dances grid (still two across), one dance with its rewards and "Do this dance", the camera, Review and Submitted. As on the video flow, the camera is the computer's webcam; that is my proposal.
The flow ends at Submitted, the page the dancer sees while the take is checked (Parts/Rewards/ActivityResult). It names the song and shows the rewards. It says nothing about whether the take will be public: the workspace_owner found that line unnecessary on 2026-10-12, the choice having just been made on Review. Done only closes the page.
Who checks, and for how long, per the workspace_owner on 2026-09-30: the owner of the dance's community checks the take privately, because there is no moderator role; the answer is pass or fail and is final; a take nobody checks within seven days of upload ends as not reviewed, which is not a fail. If it passes, the dancer qualifies for the reward either way, and the take is shown publicly only when the switch was on. If it does not pass, or is not reviewed, it is not shown, so a song only ever shows takes that really are its dance. That a private take earns the same is the intended rule, not built behaviour.
Automatic grading is deferred. A dance joins the lottery of the day it passes, and counts toward the streak for the day it was sent.
A new dance: the plus tile opens the same camera for that song. Its screens are not drawn again here; it ends in an ordinary public post (the Video sheet).
Learning the answer, two ways, per the workspace_owner on 2026-10-12, who kept the 2026-09-30 ruling and Notifications both. On the dance's own page a row above the button, "Your take", shows the state of the dancer's latest attempt at that dance: In review, Passed, Not passed or Not reviewed. Only that dancer sees it. It is drawn in the last group of this sheet. And a row in Notifications (Screens/Shell/Notifications) arrives when the answer does. Both open the same page (Parts/Rewards/ActivityResult): Submitted while in review, otherwise the result. The server keeps each take's status, visibility choice and rewards; neither route owns it. A passed, public take appears as a normal video post, in the feed and on the profile like any other.

The amendment must be ratified before implementation starts.

Differs from the specs: Spec 021 describes automatic scoring, and the Spec 024 draft asks "just a video, my new dance, or a take" at Post. Both need amending.

Under review. Handshake groups 1 to 11, Spaces groups 12 and 13, a register of every state in group 14, phone layouts in group 15, the phone route in group 16.
One Address page, in Management. It never has steps of its own: the server holds the state and the page shows it. Each card is that one page in one state, drawn as desktop content; group 15 draws the long and awkward ones on a phone, and group 16 shows how an owner reaches Address and Handles on a phone and comes back to something under way. Opening either section reads and shows what exists and never starts anything.
Handshake (Spec 012, amendments of 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-09): type the name; get one complete update for it; publish it from any Handshake wallet or service, by hand as the normal way; we watch the chain; when everything checks out the owner turns it on. A new connection has no signing step and names no wallet. A connection begun before the change keeps its signing step; that older path is noted in group 1 and kept out of the drawing.
Clocks: 14 days to publish; once seen on chain, a day for Handshake to settle it (usually about 8 hours); checks are good for thirty minutes. A missed clock never tears anything down.
Things that differ on purpose: an unclear wallet send is not a record mismatch; a mismatch is described from what was just read on chain; trouble before it is on (group 5) is not trouble after it is on (group 6). The address being on, handles being on, requests being open and members' pages working are separate facts (groups 8 and 10); pausing requests leaves issued pages working, and pages can be down while requests are open.
Spaces is two separate owner procedures. The address is one pasted signature. Names follow the spec's order: prove; prepare the space once with operate, or skip it if already prepared; wait for Spaces to record it, which is not a timer; prove again under the changed record; confirm the address; hand over; have the handover seen on Bitcoin; then agree the funding terms and open. Preparing does not open requests, confirming the address does not prove the handover, and the handover alone does not open names; only the last step does. Unused fee balance comes back on completing operator exit, not on pausing. No schedule or time is promised anywhere.
Reload: the Handshake page and the Spaces address read their state back when opened. Spaces names do not; see the dashed card in group 13.
Group 14 gives, per state, the server status, the owner's command, the evidence needed, where it leads including failures, and whether it is built, a candidate, a defect or proposed. Nothing promises a notification: none are wired.
Renewal: there is no renewal warning, per the workspace_owner. Keeping the Handshake name renewed is the owner's job; the live card says so once.
Unresolved, on purpose: the Spaces commands are illustrative and none is verified against a wallet, version and network, so none can count as executable; ending an open connection has no server command.
To draw: the verified Spaces commands, once they exist.

text:
Under review. Where a community is run. At launch that is its owner alone: Spec 010 section 7 gives both seeing and acting on moderation to the active community owner, and moderators who are not the owner are deferred. Wording on this sheet that says "moderators", and the Moderator section of the app sidebar, describe that later role and at launch mean the owner. It takes over the whole page: the app's own sidebar and bottom navigation are gone while it is open, and a close mark leaves it and returns to the community. It is opened from the community's More menu (Manage) and from the Moderator section of the app sidebar.
Sections, in this order. Moderation: Queue. Community: Profile, Address, Handles, Rules, Links. Safety: AI moderation, Telegram, Assistant. A person sees only the sections they are allowed to use.
On desktop the sections are a sidebar that stays in view, with the close mark and the community at its top, and the chosen section fills the page. On phone the first screen is the list of sections with the close mark; a section opens as its own page with a back arrow and its name centred. A page that opens from a section on the phone is a second column on desktop.
Queue: two lists, Dances and Reports, oldest first, both the owner's alone at launch. For a dance, per the workspace_owner on 2026-09-30: only the community's owner passes or fails it, never the dancer themselves, and the server checks that authority again when the answer is saved. A dance opens full screen, laid out like a feed video with the dancer and song at the bottom left, the dance it is meant to match in the top right corner, and Fail and Pass. The next one opens after a decision and the dancer is told in Notifications. A dance leaves the list unanswered seven days after upload, and the dancer is told it was not reviewed. A report shows the post, what it was reported for and how many times, and Keep and Hide.
AI moderation: every post is checked before it publishes. Six kinds, each set to Allow, Review or Block; a row opens the three choices and the change saves at once. Review sends the post to the Queue. One line lists what is always blocked and cannot be changed.
Telegram: before connecting, one field for the bot's token and Connect. After, the bot, the channel (tap to change), a switch to post new content, a button to share the latest 20 posts, and Disconnect.
Assistant: saving is as built. Every change is a draft and nothing is kept until Save; the page shows Saving, saved, a failure, and the case where the settings changed in another session. Each key saves apart from the draft with its own Check and save. Every built setting is kept: voice replies, the ElevenLabs key, the voice, the voice model, when to reply with voice and the speech characters a day sit on a Voice page. Remembering chats for a day is ours; what OpenRouter, the model's provider and ElevenLabs keep is theirs and is said separately.
Profile, Rules and Links are proposed: the server holds and shows these, with no command to change them. A rule has a title, a body, a report reason, a position and an active or archived status, so its editor has all four fields, moving up and down, and Remove meaning archive. Links are loose data on the server, so name and address are assumed.
Archive is not drawn. The workspace_owner said on 2026-10-12 to do whatever is easiest on the existing API, and the API has no way to archive a community, so the section is left out. That is the design agent's choice and does not settle what archiving would mean. The app still lists Archive with no page.
Address and Handles are on Flows/Community/Address.
The dance check follows the workspace_owner's rulings of 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-09 and is part of launch as of 2026-10-12. The written spec says the first release has no dance grading and no moderator queue for ordinary videos, so the Spec 021 amendment must be ratified before this is built. Ordinary posts still publish by themselves.
To decide: whether a failed dancer may be told why (the 2026-09-30 draft says there is no reviewer note); what a hidden post's author sees; whether six kinds is enough (the app has thirteen, the extra seven being the severe forms); whether Telegram needs the list of what was sent.
To draw: choosing a model and a voice; choosing a Telegram channel; empty lists; hidden posts and restoring one; what someone who is not the owner sees on reaching this page by a link (access denied); a dance nearing its seven days.
